pages.text: "Slipping again!" Bung pulled a sack cord onto little horns. Grandpa loaded his tied boat, carrying two sacks on big horns in long strides.
Bung wanted to carry like Grandpa. "Two sacks for me too!" But the cords slipped straight off.
Bung tried again and again. Each time, thump! Sacks on the floor. Ddori pointed at them.
Bung sat at the edge and touched the horns. Only two fingers long! "Why are mine so small?"
Grandpa sat beside Bung with a hand on those horns. "Upset because the sacks slipped?" Bung watched the knees. "Yours are big."
"What could hang on Ddori's horns?" he asked. Only one finger long, nothing could hang yet. Standing together: small, next size, big.
"Horns widen as you grow. This fits yours now." Grandpa hung a light basket on Bung's horns. "My little horns are mine!"
Bung drew Ddori's hand close and strode along the walkway. The basket never slipped! Bung's shoulders rose proudly.
Now Bung knew three things for loading. "One, hang what fits my horns! Two, if it will not hang, use both hands! Three, call Grandpa if heavy!" Ddori picked up fallen fruit. My little horns are mine!
At sunset, Grandpa lifted Bung in a hug. "Your basket reached the boat first today." Bung patted the horns and smiled. "My little horns are mine!"
